knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for C and C++. Loaded automatically when agents work on .cpp, .cc, .cxx, .c, .h, .hpp, or .hxx files, or CMakeLists.txt. Applies to C++20, systems programming, embedded, game engines, and high-performance computing.

core-principles.principle: Every resource (memory, files, locks, sockets) is owned by an object whose destructor releases it. No manual cleanup code outside destructors.
Never use new/delete directly. Use smart pointers and containers for all heap allocation.
Pass and return by value; rely on move semantics and copy elision for performance.
Use constexpr, static_assert, concepts, and templates to catch errors at compile time.
Build with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror; every warning is a latent bug.

guardrail.rule: Never use new/delete directly. Use std::make_unique or std::make_shared for all heap allocation.
guardrail.good: auto user = std::make_unique<User>("alice"); // RAII: destructor called automatically on scope exit

guardrail.rule: Never use raw owning pointers. Raw pointers are only valid as non-owning observers.
Build with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror and sanitizers (-fsanitize=address,undefined) in debug builds. Every warning is a latent bug.
Never use using namespace std; in headers. It pollutes every translation unit that includes the header. Allowed in .cpp function scope only.
Move constructors and move assignment operators MUST be noexcept. Non-noexcept moves prevent std::vector from using move optimization.
Always catch by const reference: catch (const std::exception& e). Never catch by value (slices) or non-const reference.
All concurrent code must pass ThreadSanitizer (-fsanitize=thread). Never hold a lock while calling a callback or virtual function (deadlock risk).
Prefer enum class over plain enum. Scoped enums avoid implicit conversions and name collisions.
Use std::optional<T> for values that may be absent. Never use sentinel values (-1, nullptr, "") to signal absence.
Run clang-format and clang-tidy before every commit. No manual style exceptions.

standard-compiler.item: Use C++20 as the minimum standard (-std=c++20 / CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
Compile with at least -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic; treat warnings as errors (-Werror)
Use static_assert to verify assumptions about types, sizes, and alignments
Set CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON for clang-tidy and IDE integration
Pin compiler minimum version in CI (e.g., GCC 12+, Clang 15+, MSVC 19.34+)

code-style.item: Run clang-format before every commit (no exceptions)
Run clang-tidy with project checks before every commit
snake_case for functions, variables, namespaces, file names
PascalCase for types (classes, structs, enums, concepts, type aliases)
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for macros and compile-time constants
Prefer enum class over plain enum (scoped, no implicit conversion)
Header include order: own header, project headers, third-party, standard library
Use #pragma once or traditional include guards consistently (pick one)
No using namespace std; in headers (allowed in .cpp function scope only)

memory-management.item: Default to stack allocation; heap allocate only when lifetime or size requires it
std::unique_ptr for single ownership (default smart pointer)
std::shared_ptr only when ownership is genuinely shared; document why
Use std::make_unique and std::make_shared (exception-safe, single allocation)
Containers (std::vector, std::string, std::array) manage their own memory
Use std::span for non-owning views into contiguous memory
Use std::string_view for non-owning string references (read-only, no allocation)

error-handling.item: Use exceptions for truly exceptional conditions (constructor failure, precondition violations)
Use std::optional<T> for values that may be absent (replaces sentinel values)
Use std::variant<T, Error> or std::expected<T, E> (C++23) for result types
Mark functions noexcept when they do not throw (enables move optimization)
Always catch by const reference: catch (const std::exception& e)
Never catch ... without rethrowing or logging (swallowed errors are bugs)

concurrency.item: Prefer std::jthread over std::thread (automatic join, stop token support)
Protect shared mutable state with std::mutex and std::scoped_lock
Use std::atomic for lock-free shared counters and flags
Never hold a lock while calling a callback or virtual function (deadlock risk)
All concurrent code must pass ThreadSanitizer (-fsanitize=thread)
Prefer std::latch, std::barrier, std::counting_semaphore (C++20) for coordination

directory.purpose: Entry point (thin: parse args, call run)

project-structure.note: main.cpp should be thin: parse arguments, build config, call into library code. One class per header/source pair.

pattern.name: CMakeLists.txt Essentials
pattern.example:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20) project(myproject VERSION 0.1.0 LANGUAGES CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20) set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON) set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF) set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON)
add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror)
if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug") add_compile_options(-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer) add_link_options(-fsanitize=address,undefined) endif()
add_subdirectory(src) add_subdirectory(tests)

rules.rule: Test names describe behavior: TEST(OrderService, CancelledOrderCannotBeShipped)
Use TEST_F with fixtures for shared setup/teardown
EXPECT_* for non-fatal assertions; ASSERT_* only when continuation is meaningless
Mock external dependencies with interfaces and dependency injection
Run tests under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer in CI

knowledge-base.clang-format-config: # .clang-format BasedOnStyle: Google IndentWidth: 4 ColumnLimit: 100 PointerAlignment: Left SortIncludes: CaseInsensitive
knowledge-base.clang-tidy-config: # .clang-tidy Checks: > -*, bugprone-*, cert-*, cppcoreguidelines-*, misc-*, modernize-*, performance-*, readability-*, -modernize-use-trailing-return-type WarningsAsErrors: '*' HeaderFilterRegex: 'src/.*'

sanitizers.note: ASan + UBSan run together; TSan and MSan must run separately. Always use -fno-omit-frame-pointer with sanitizers.

quick-reference.item: std::make_unique (single owner) or std::make_shared (shared); never new/delete
exceptions for exceptional; std::expected<T,E> for expected failures
snake_case functions/vars, PascalCase types, SCREAMING for macros
C++20 minimum; concepts, ranges, jthread, std::span available
